post.description:
ARCH-2 §5.4's self-service counterpart to HR's Reset Password button
— the two "converge on one internal function" (auth_tokens.issue_temporary_password).
Always 204, no matter what: unknown email, disabled account, an account
with no linked Employee record (nowhere to send the email — the whole
temp-password/email mechanism is Employee-centric, same boundary
HR-initiated reset already has), or rate-limited — every branch below
is a silent no-op. Anything else would make this endpoint an
account-enumeration oracle, the exact failure mode ARCH-2 calls out by
name.

Employee §2.3's forced-change-on-first-login flow (must_change_password
is set True by create_login/reset_password) had no way to ever complete —
found by the Phase 2 audit: nothing anywhere ever cleared the flag. Any
logged-in user may change their own password here; no RBAC screen gate
since this isn't a screen, it's every account's own credential.

put.description:
§4.1: "add PUT .../{id}... make Start Date editable... make End Date
an entered field." §4.1 also says "Keep the lock rules" — Invariant 4
freezes a locked year for everyone including Super Admin, and editing its
own start/end dates is exactly the kind of write that rule exists to
block, so this checks status the same way lock/set-current already do
rather than carving out an exception for itself.

Label is re-derived from the (possibly new) start_date, same rule as
create — a Financial Year's label always means "the calendar year it
starts in," never a stored, independently-editable string.

delete.description:
Masters §3.0/§3.1's own Status & Deletion Rule (01-masters-module.md):
"A Financial Year with no records referencing it anywhere in the CMS may
be deleted outright... Once any record in any module references it,
deletion is disabled and Locking becomes the only further action
available." `reference_count` (models/numbering.py) is exactly this
counter — incremented elsewhere whenever another module snapshots this
year's id, never here.

post.description:
A002 revisited: locking is no longer categorically one-way — Super
Admin has an explicit, RBAC-gated override. See migration 0009's
docstring for the full reasoning; the short version is that
`trg_fy_reject_unlock` still rejects any UPDATE that flips `locked` back
to `open` UNLESS the current DB session has set `@fy_unlock_allowed = 1`,
and this endpoint is the only place in the codebase that ever sets it —
so a stray script or a different service still can't do this by
accident, only this one sanctioned, permission-checked path can.

Reopening genuinely reopens the period: every module that checks "is this
FY locked" before allowing a write (Invoice, Payroll, Expense, ...) will
once again permit edits to records dated inside it, exactly as if it had
never been locked. This is the real, system-wide consequence a Super
Admin is accepting — not a cosmetic status flip on this one screen.

Every downstream module that snapshots a financial_year_id on create
(Employee, Salary Structure, Leave, Attendance, ...) resolves "today's
FY" from the one row flagged is_current — see
app.services.numbering.get_current_financial_year. Unset-then-set, same
single-active-row order as every other one-active-row guard in this
schema (Work Week Policy, Pay Cycle, ...).

head's Applies Until to the day before the change, then add a new head
(usually via Duplicate) with the new figures." The caller supplies the
new figures (typically the old ones with a new rate + Applies From); this

calculation would call the engine, so this endpoint doubles as a live
proof that the isolated tax_engine module is wired correctly end to end.

get.description:
Employee §2.10 Employee Dashboard — the landing screen right after
login. Widgets per §2.10's table: leave balance snapshot (§2.4), latest
payslip mini-card (§2.5), open tickets/pending tasks/assigned assets
counts (§2.7/§2.8/§2.9), a company announcements mini feed (§2.11),
a recent activity feed (this project's Notification rows are exactly the
"system-generated entries" §2.10 describes), and quick links into every
self-service screen.

Gated on employee.my_profile (mode "full" for all 5 roles, per the
registry's own "always own scope in practice" comment) rather than a new
screen — §2.10 itself says "All 5 roles" with only the Manager strip
varying, the same self-service-baseline shape my_profile already governs.

Manager's "My Team" strip (§2.10, additive) is gated on the caller's
actual role, not perms.mode — every role's employee.my_profile mode is
"full", so mode alone can't distinguish a Manager here the way it does
on Directory/Master Record.

post.description:
Reverses disable-login (Employee §2.2: Disable is a toggle, distinct
from a stronger, separate "remove access" action) — found missing by the
Phase 2 audit: disable_login had no way back, permanently locking out
anyone disabled by mistake, since create_login also refuses to run again
once employee.user_id is set.

Employee §2.2's "Reset Password" button — generates a fresh temporary
password and forces a change on next login. Found missing entirely by
the Phase 2 audit. Same "HR never sees the password" rule as
create_login — Phase 6 emails it instead of returning it.

The seeded "password_reset" template's only placeholder is
{{reset_link}} (a click-a-link flow) but this endpoint's actual flow has
never generated a reset link/token — it issues a temporary password, the
same mechanism create_login uses. Rather than inventing a new
token/URL scheme not asked for here, the temporary password is passed
through the template's existing {{reset_link}} placeholder — the
"same info that was being returned" before, just emailed instead of
returned. If a genuine link-based reset flow is ever built, this call
site is the one to revisit.

schema.title: Response List Onboarding Items Api V1 Employees  Employee Id  Onboarding Get

get.description:
HR/Super Admin's cross-employee onboarding queue (prototype's
emp.onboardqueue) — every employee currently mid-onboarding, i.e. whose
onboarding_checklist_items don't yet have every step COMPLETE or
SKIPPED. `employee.onboarding` has has_scope=False (screens.py:140) —
same as the per-employee GET /employees/{id}/onboarding this reuses the
checklist data of — so require_screen(ONBOARDING) alone is the right
gate, no apply_scope needed.

Built by grouping OnboardingChecklistItem rows in Python rather than a
GROUP BY/HAVING query: at 7 rows/employee this is a small in-memory
fan-out, and the "oldest incomplete step" figure (lowest-ordinal PENDING
item) needs the individual rows anyway, not just aggregate counts.

Department is an OUTER join deliberately, not an inner one — an
employee whose department_id fails to resolve to a live Department row
(a data-integrity gap, not this endpoint's concern) must still surface
here rather than silently vanish from HR's onboarding queue; found live
while verifying this endpoint against the dev DB, where every seeded
employee's department_id turned out to be a stale id no current
Department row has (confirmed separately from this task's own scope).

get.description:
§2.2's "Download" button (self-service) and §2.3's "View" (Accountant/
HR/Super Admin) both resolve to this one formatted, letterheaded
document, per the OFFICIAL DOCUMENT RULE (Appendix B) — gated here by
ownership OR the admin screen, the same self-or-admin shape
employee_lifecycle.py's withdraw_resignation already uses.

post.description:
§2.3 / A119: recalculation OR manual figure adjustment, a required
Reason either way, and a Reissue History entry (old figures alongside
new). Recalculation reuses the SAME calculation pass Run Payroll itself
uses (payroll_runs._calculate_employee), so a reissue can never drift
from how a fresh run would compute the same period.

§6.1 "Require Super Admin Approval to Reissue a Payslip" — OFF by
default (Accountant/HR reissue directly, the historical behavior).
ON: reissuing is restricted to Super Admin outright, rather than a genuine
async "Accountant/HR requests, Super Admin approves later" queue —
deliberately narrower than the doc's own "sign-off first" phrasing, and
disclosed as such rather than silently built as something it isn't. The
async version is blocked by two existing CHECK constraints from this
table's original migration (0004_payroll.py): ck_reissue_approval
requires approved_by to be set WHENEVER approval_required is true — so a
row can never represent "required but not yet given" at insert time —
and ck_payslip_status allows only ('PROCESSED','REISSUED'), no third
"reissue pending" state for the payslip itself to sit in while it waits.
payslip_reissues is also append-only (trg_reissue_append_only), so there
is no later UPDATE that could add an approval after the fact either.
Widening either constraint is a real migration touching a live-money
table's existing rows, not something to do as a side effect of one
toggle — Super-Admin-only reissuing is what §6.1's actual schema
supports today: the approval IS Super Admin being the one who acts.

post.description:
Schema-ready since Phase 4 (InvoicePayment.status/reversed_at/
reversed_by/reversal_reason) but never wired to an endpoint — closes
that gap. Deliberately NOT available once PAID: the invoice is locked
at that point (trg_invoices_no_unlock blocks any status un-set at the
storage layer, defense in depth against exactly this), so undoing a
payment that already locked the invoice goes through a Credit Note like
every other post-lock correction, never a reversal. PEND_PAID (§6.2's
second-approval gate) IS reversible — nothing is locked yet there, and
catching a mis-recorded payment before Super Admin confirms is exactly
what this exists for.

§6.2 "Require Second Approval Before an Invoice Locks as Paid" — the
confirmation step itself. Only reachable from PEND_PAID; confirming
moves the invoice to PAID and locks it, same as an unconfirmed payment
would have done directly with the toggle off.

post.description:
§2.8's "Deferred on the team view: bulk approve (approval is per
entry as built)" — reversed here, same reasoning as Bugs' Overdue/Created
On range: not a technical blocker, just not yet built. Authorization is
resolved ONCE against this project (unlike the single-entry endpoint,
which isn't project-scoped and so re-fetches the project per call) —
same Lead-of-this-project-regardless-of-role OR Manager/Super Admin rule
as approve_timesheet_entry. Partial success by design: an entry that
isn't Submitted (already approved by someone else, mid-batch) is
skipped, not a 409 for the whole batch — a concurrent-approval race is
an expected case for a bulk action, not an error.

get.description:
§2.8 "Filters, on both lists — added in this revision... Projects:
Project Status (multi-select), Service Category (from Masters), Customer,
and a date range on project start." Service Category is skipped — Project
has no such field, the same genuinely-absent dimension already confirmed
on Customer's and Opportunity's own directories, not a build gap here.

put.description:
§2.2: "Status and Assigned To are locked after creation... every
change is captured in Assignment History" — this endpoint only ever
touches the Details tab's Core Info + Purchase & Financial fields (§6.1),
never Status/Assigned To, and never Location/Department either — those
two live only under Assignment & Location (§6.1), edited exclusively via
PUT /assets/{id}/location, which shares the 'assign' action (Super
Admin + HR) rather than this 'edit' action (Super Admin + Accountant),
so Accountant can never relocate an asset through this endpoint.

get.description:
§2.9 Asset Card: "a single-page printable summary: Asset Tag, Name,
Category, Assigned To, Purchase Date. Purchase Value and Current Value
are included only for roles that can already see those fields." Reuses
_load_asset_out's masking (and _get_asset_scoped's team-scope check) so
this can never show a Manager more than the record's own JSON response
already would.

put.description:
§2.4's own disclosed gap, now closed: "add and edit entries" was only
ever half-built (add only) — this is the missing update, same edit-action
guard (Accountant + Super Admin) as add_maintenance above. Exists
specifically so a system-generated entry (created by an approved Repair/
Damage request, §2.6, with Cost/Next Due Date left blank) can actually be
filled in later, which is the concrete case §2.4's own text names.

AssetLocationWrite.description:
§6.1: Assignment & Location fields are edited only through this
2.3-family action (Super Admin directly, HR "via Assign/Transfer/
Unassign only") — never through the general Details-tab edit action,
which Accountant also holds and must not be able to use to relocate
an asset.

BankAccountUpdate.title: BankAccountUpdate
BankAccountUpdate.description:
Editing an existing account. account_number is included (accounts do
occasionally need correcting, e.g. a typo caught after saving) and still
goes through A009's Confirm Account Number check whenever it's supplied;
is_default/is_active are deliberately excluded — those have their own
dedicated endpoints with their own guard logic (set-default, deactivate).
